text: Found it: in `src/plugin/timezone/index.js`, `dayjs.tz(input, timezone)` always runs the input through `d.utc(input)`, so a numeric timestamp, a JS `Date`, or a Day.js object is treated as a UTC wall-clock time instead of an instant, giving a wrong offset/value. Fix: for non-string inputs, delegate to `d(input).tz(timezone)`. Applying and verifying now (baseline + full suite across several TZs).
Investigating the `Z`-token bug in the timezone plugin with a differential test against moment-timezone (the repo's own reference). Fix and verification in progress.

Found it: `src/locale/nl.js` uses `ordinal: n => `${n}.``, so `Do` renders "1."…"31." instead of the Dutch ordinal ("1ste", "2e", … "20ste"). Fixing the ordinal to match Moment's Dutch locale and verifying Do for 1–31.

Found it: `weekYear()` only handles the "December belongs to next week-year" case; it is missing the symmetric "early January belongs to the previous week-year" case (e.g. 2016-01-01 is ISO week 53 of 2015 with `yearStart: 4`). Adding that branch and verifying against moment for 2010–2025.

Found it: the `A`/`a` tokens in `customParseFormat` only match hard-coded English `AM`/`PM` and ignore the locale's `meridiem` function, so locales with their own meridiem strings can't be parsed. Replacing them with a locale-aware `meridiemMatch` and verifying.

Fixed and verified. `dayjs.tz(input, timezone)` now delegates to `d(input).tz(timezone)` for non-string inputs (numeric timestamp, JS `Date`, Day.js object), so they are treated as instants instead of UTC wall-clock times. Verified against moment-timezone: `dayjs.tz(1401638400000|new Date(...)|dayjs(...), 'America/New_York')` now matches moment on format(), utcOffset() and valueOf(); string-input parsing is unchanged; full suite green (no regressions).

Fixed and verified. `src/locale/nl.js` now uses the Dutch ordinal (1ste, 2de, … 8ste, … 20ste, … 31ste) instead of "1."…"31.", matching Moment's `nl` locale exactly (including the `[...]` escaping convention the repo uses so the ordinal text isn't re-parsed as format tokens). `format('Do')` for days 1–31 now matches moment for all 31 days; locale tests and the full suite stay green.

Fixed and verified. `weekYear()` was missing the symmetric case for early January: a date in January that belongs to the last week of the previous week-year (e.g. 2016-01-01 with `yearStart: 4` is week 53 of 2015) now returns `year - 1`. Checked every day from 2010-01-01 to 2025-12-31 for locales `en` and `en-gb` against moment: 16 mismatches before, 0 after; existing weekYear/weekOfYear tests and the full suite stay green.

Fixed and verified. The `A`/`a` tokens in `customParseFormat` no longer hard-code English `AM`/`PM`: they now use a locale-aware `meridiemMatch` that consults `locale.meridiem` (falling back to the English comparison when the locale has none). Parsing e.g. `dayjs('2018-01-01 上午 12:00', 'YYYY-MM-DD A hh:mm', locale)` now yields 00:00 and `下午 12:00` yields 12:00, for both `A` and `a`; all 38 pre-existing customParseFormat tests and the full suite stay green.

Fixed and verified. `unitToMS` in `src/plugin/duration/index.js` was missing a `milliseconds` entry, so `dayjs.duration(n, 'milliseconds')` / `'ms'` computed `n * undefined` → NaN (toISOString() gave 'P0D'). Added `milliseconds: 1`; `dayjs.duration(100, 'milliseconds').toISOString()` is now 'PT0.1S', `.asMilliseconds()` is 100, `.milliseconds()` is 500 for 1500 ms, and the existing duration tests plus the full suite stay green.

Fixed and verified. In `proto.tz` the offset was computed as `(this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60`, but `toLocaleString` has no milliseconds, so any instance with a non-zero ms part produced a fractional `$offset` and `format('Z')` rendered garbage (e.g. `-07:0.0020499999999969987` instead of `-07:00`; `format('ZZ')` was likewise broken and `utcOffset()` non-integer). It is now `Math.round(...)`. Differential test vs moment-timezone over 8 zones × 6 millisecond-bearing timestamps: 165 mismatches before → 0 for `format()`, `format('Z')`, `format('ZZ')` and `utcOffset()` after; the timezone suite (14 tests) and the full suite stay green.
